Hello, i wanna optimize you(Ai) to use any available gpu before you decide to use my cpu. I wanna do this for performance so i'm able to do other tasks while i wait for your response. How can make check and use a valid gpu for your processing in python? This is the script i use:

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM
import chatHandler
import sys

model_name = "Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct" 

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name)

def main(file_name, message):

    chat_history = chatHandler.messages(file_name, message)

    inputs = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
        chat_history,
        add_generation_prompt=True,
        tokenize=True,
        return_dict=True,
        return_tensors="pt",
    ).to(model.device)

    output = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=800)
    generated_answer = tokenizer.decode(
        output[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1]:],
        skip_special_tokens=True
    )

    chatHandler.preserve_chat(file_name, generated_answer, False, False)

    print(generated_answer)

if __name__ == "__main__" :
    main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])

To optimize your script to use a GPU if one is available, you can leverage PyTorch or TensorFlow, which are commonly used with Hugging Face models. Below is an updated version of your script that checks for available GPUs and uses them if available.

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM
import chatHandler
import sys

# Set device to GPU if available, otherwise set to CPU
device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

model_name = "Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device)

def main(file_name, message):
    chat_history = chatHandler.messages(file_name, message)
    
    inputs = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
        chat_history,
        add_generation_prompt=True,
        tokenize=True,
        return_dict=True,
        return_tensors="pt",
    ).to(device)

    output = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=800)
    generated_answer = tokenizer.decode(
        output[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1]:],
        skip_special_tokens=True
    )
    
    chatHandler.preserve_chat(file_name, generated_answer, False, False)
    
    print(generated_answer)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])
```

This script first checks if a GPU is available using `torch.cuda.is_available()`. If a GPU is available, it sets the device to the GPU (`torch.device("cuda")`), otherwise, it defaults to the CPU (`torch.device("cpu")`). The model and tokenizer are then moved to the appropriate device.
